hyperedges.label: Findings that are all 'a fix applied to some of N equivalent paths'
Capabilities the Android background service lacked
Four execution contexts writing one vault under inconsistent locking

nodes.label: Audit of the 0.4.x batch — findings and outcomes
nodes.rationale: Written 2026-08-22 after 0.4.2 shipped; a systematic adversarial audit of all 46 commits, several findings created by that week's own fixes interacting. Everything is either fixed with a test proven to fail on the previous code, or explicitly recorded as not a bug.
nodes.norm_label: audit of the 0.4.x batch — findings and outcomes

nodes.label: Failure shape 1: a fix applied to some of N equivalent paths
nodes.rationale: The vault is written by four contexts — UI isolate, worker isolate, Android background service, CLI — so a fix that lands in one is invisible in the others.
nodes.norm_label: failure shape 1: a fix applied to some of n equivalent paths

nodes.label: Failure shape 2: 'absent' read as 'current'
nodes.rationale: A field that was never written defaults to today's value, so stale data claims to be fresh.

nodes.label: Failure shape 3: a read-side guard with no write-side counterpart
nodes.rationale: The thing the read guard protects against is laundered back in through an unguarded write path.
nodes.norm_label: failure shape 3: a read-side guard with no write-side counterpart

nodes.label: Execution context: UI / root isolate
nodes.rationale: Has donor publish and the orphan temp sweep; holds the VaultLock only across syncNow, and resolveConflict holds none.

nodes.label: Execution context: worker isolate
nodes.rationale: Writes the index, the donor and the search index under no VaultLock; a VaultSyncWorker timeout destroys the engine without Dart's finally, stranding the lock for up to the 10-minute stale window.

nodes.label: Execution context: Android background service
nodes.rationale: The process most likely to be killed mid-write, and the reason the temp-file grace period exists, yet it never swept temps and kept the vault-wide conflict gate after the foreground dropped it.

nodes.label: Execution context: CLI (tylog)
nodes.rationale: Scans with CliTypstInspector but originally published no donor; tylog dedupe ran with no inspector at all while deciding which files to delete.

nodes.label: Capability / mechanism: orphan temp-file sweep
nodes.rationale: Atomic writes leave .tmp/.backup orphans on interrupted writes; sweeping at vault open after an hour untouched avoids deleting a live in-flight write.

nodes.label: Capability: VaultLock
nodes.rationale: Locking is inconsistent across the four writers; pre-existing and bounded, and needs a heartbeat rather than a one-line change.

nodes.label: SyncCursor
nodes.rationale: An unbound cursor carries a server-generated etag, so against a different server it simply fails to match and the pass re-decides correctly — which is why absent schema/remoteKey is not a real risk.

nodes.label: remoteSnapshot
nodes.rationale: A remote-deleted record keeps its snapshot as evidence, not as a live side — reading it without checking remoteExists offers deleted content as a resolvable choice.

nodes.label: P0-1: 'Keep Nextcloud's version' could delete the file it claimed to keep
nodes.rationale: The dialog read remoteSnapshot without checking remoteExists; when the snapshot was a superset of local the default preselected it with 'loses nothing' while the resolve deleted the local file.
nodes.norm_label: p0-1: 'keep nextcloud's version' could delete the file it claimed to keep

nodes.label: P0-2: background service still suspended the whole vault on one conflict
nodes.rationale: Self-perpetuating: the repairs that clear such a record all live inside sync(), behind the very gate that blocks it.
nodes.norm_label: p0-2: background service still suspended the whole vault on one conflict

nodes.label: P0-3: self-heal compared two frozen snapshots and deleted live conflicts
nodes.rationale: Record written local A / remote B, user edits to C, a peer uploads A → record deleted, C never uploaded, 'Conflict resolved' on screen. Fixed by comparing the live file against the live remote.
nodes.norm_label: p0-3: self-heal compared two frozen snapshots and deleted live conflicts

nodes.label: P0-4: bulk resolve reported 'Resolved N' over an untouched vault
nodes.rationale: It decided each step by reading syncError, a slot shared with sync, and a not-ready config made resolveConflict return silently.
nodes.norm_label: p0-4: bulk resolve reported 'resolved n' over an untouched vault

nodes.label: P1-5: reusable ignored queryVersion, laundering facts through the donor
nodes.rationale: Reuse is still allowed because the derived half is fine; only the unvouchable query facts are dropped.
nodes.norm_label: p1-5: reusable ignored queryversion, laundering facts through the donor

nodes.label: P1-6: failed inspect kept old-byte metadata under the new fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Stamping stale metadata with the new file's fingerprint and hash makes it permanently authoritative — and it was donated to other devices.
nodes.norm_label: p1-6: failed inspect kept old-byte metadata under the new fingerprint

nodes.label: P1-7: donor prune and donor load asked different questions
nodes.rationale: Donors were kept forever by the prune predicate and read never by the load predicate.
nodes.norm_label: p1-7: donor prune and donor load asked different questions

nodes.label: P1-10: a failed save was discarded if the user kept typing
nodes.rationale: Edit gone, UI still showing a save pending — a silent data loss dressed as progress.
nodes.norm_label: p1-10: a failed save was discarded if the user kept typing

nodes.label: P2-11: CLI rewrote both indexes unconditionally and dedupe ran with no inspector
nodes.rationale: tylog dedupe decided which files to delete from a scan that had no Typst inspector behind it.
nodes.norm_label: p2-11: cli rewrote both indexes unconditionally and dedupe ran with no inspector

nodes.label: P2-12: only the UI swept orphaned temp files
nodes.rationale: The background service is the process most likely to be killed mid-write — the reason the grace period exists — and it never swept.
nodes.norm_label: p2-12: only the ui swept orphaned temp files

nodes.label: P2-13: _sweepSafBackups and pruneUnusable wrapped a whole loop in one catch
nodes.rationale: One locked file skipped everything after it, forever — per-item work needs per-item error handling.
nodes.norm_label: p2-13: _sweepsafbackups and pruneunusable wrapped a whole loop in one catch

nodes.label: P2-14: IndexDonorStore.publish swallowed every failure
nodes.rationale: The exact way the donor mechanism died silently for days before.

nodes.label: P2-15: search index had no derivation stamp
nodes.rationale: A derive-only bump left search holding pre-fold tags forever, because an unstamped file reads as current.
nodes.norm_label: p2-15: search index had no derivation stamp

nodes.label: P3: three tests asserted nothing
nodes.rationale: An anti-test that would pass with the feature deleted, a guard test with no positive control, and an assertion on a variable the test set itself.

nodes.label: Not a bug: absent schema/remoteKey in sync_state.json read as current
nodes.rationale: Looks exactly like shape 2, but both safe-looking fixes are worse: rejecting the file discards a deliberate tested migration, and treating it as recovered hands the user a conflict per file on the first sync after upgrading. The risk is also not real because an unbound cursor carries a server-generated etag. Recorded in the code at the check itself.
nodes.norm_label: not a bug: absent schema/remotekey in sync_state.json read as current

nodes.label: Open: locking is inconsistent across writers
nodes.rationale: A VaultSyncWorker timeout destroys the engine without Dart's finally, stranding the lock for up to the 10-minute stale window; a rebuild longer than that lets the UI barge in mid-run. Needs a heartbeat, not a one-line change.
nodes.norm_label: open: locking is inconsistent across writers

nodes.label: Open: fallback-inspected notes are never retried on unchanged bytes
nodes.rationale: Deliberate — retrying known-bad notes would spend the whole inspection budget every scan — but a transient engine failure is sticky until the next edit or a forced rebuild.
nodes.norm_label: open: fallback-inspected notes are never retried on unchanged bytes

nodes.label: Conflict self-heal
nodes.rationale: Must compare the live local file against the live remote, never two frozen snapshots, or it deletes conflicts that are still real.

nodes.label: Donor reuse (inherit facts instead of recompiling)
nodes.norm_label: donor reuse (inherit facts instead of recompiling)

nodes.label: Query/derive version split
nodes.rationale: Bump queryVersion only when the Typst query itself changes; a derive-only bump then re-derives from donor data instead of recompiling, which is precisely the case where reuse matters most.

nodes.label: Query facts (re-derivation facts carried per note)
nodes.rationale: Raw queried records stored alongside the derived NoteRef so a version bump can re-derive; only vouchable facts (matching queryVersion) may be exported.
nodes.norm_label: query facts (re-derivation facts carried per note)

nodes.label: Conflict auto-resolution (fast-forward and identical-content rules)
nodes.rationale: Resolve without asking only where no information can be lost, and never silently — every auto-resolution is logged with its rule name and counted in the dashboard.

nodes.label: Regenerable cache paths
nodes.rationale: A conflict on a file that can simply be refetched or rebuilt (index, donor, search index) should auto-clear and refetch rather than gate the vault — proven by the A24 clearing a conflict on the donor file itself on launch.

nodes.label: Hardware verification on P30 and A24 after the 0.4.x batch
nodes.rationale: Index version 10 / query 1 on both; 6,207 of 6,215 notes Typst-queried; fallback 8 (0.13%), down from 432/4,225 (10%) on the A24; zero pending conflicts.
nodes.norm_label: hardware verification on p30 and a24 after the 0.4.x batch

nodes.label: A24 self-recovery: donor conflict cleared, cache-refetched, v10 by inheritance
nodes.rationale: Four and a half minutes by inheriting 6,207 sets of facts rather than recompiling, against fourteen minutes for a from-scratch rebuild.
nodes.norm_label: a24 self-recovery: donor conflict cleared, cache-refetched, v10 by inheritance

nodes.label: Sync conflict recovery — scope of work
nodes.rationale: Kept after completion because the live-incident analysis is the reason each fix looks the way it does.
nodes.norm_label: sync conflict recovery — scope of work

nodes.label: A24 incident: 695 articles behind for four hours
nodes.rationale: App running, network fine; five junk conflicts (three docs.astral.sh redirect stubs, one coqui.ai 404, one real daily note) froze the entire device's sync.
nodes.norm_label: a24 incident: 695 articles behind for four hours

nodes.label: Vault-wide conflict gate ('Sync is paused until you review the conflicts')
nodes.rationale: Any pending conflict suspended automatic sync for every path, including the 500 pending downloads that had nothing to do with it.
nodes.norm_label: vault-wide conflict gate ('sync is paused until you review the conflicts')

nodes.label: Phase 1: the conflict gate becomes per-path
nodes.rationale: The single highest-value change: it alone would have prevented the four-hour stall. Conflicted paths are skipped; everything else syncs.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1: the conflict gate becomes per-path

nodes.label: Phase 2: auto-resolve the provably-lossless cases
nodes.rationale: Most conflicts are not real disagreements; resolve without asking but only where no information can be lost, and log every auto-resolution with its rule name — never silent.

nodes.label: Rule 1: identical content, different ETag/mtime
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 equal on both sides → adopt the remote cursor and drop the conflict; the drain re-uploading byte-identical files was a large share of the incident.

nodes.label: Rule 2: fast-forward (one side a strict superset)
nodes.rationale: Append-only edit — keep the longer side; lossless by definition. Exactly the daily/2026-08-19.typ case (remote 184 bytes, local 294, identical up to the appended == Reading block).
nodes.norm_label: rule 2: fast-forward (one side a strict superset)

nodes.label: Rule 3 (dropped): pipeline-authoritative articles
nodes.rationale: Dropped as unsound: import_sha256 hashes the upstream markdown, not the note file, so it cannot prove the absence of local edits.

nodes.label: Phase 3a: a resolve announces itself and reports on the remote write
nodes.rationale: Resolution is complete once the remote write and snapshot cleanup land; awaiting refreshIndex(always: true) made a ten-minute wait indistinguishable from a dead button.
nodes.norm_label: phase 3a: a resolve announces itself and reports on the remote write

nodes.label: Phase 3b: rewrite a deleted-remote conflict to the delete-vs-changed shape
nodes.rationale: Proven on the A24: the record held remoteExists true, the file was deleted server-side, the guard threw 'Nextcloud changed again' on every attempt, and _refreshConflictRemote was reachable only when remoteFile != null — so a deleted remote could never refresh and gated auto-sync forever.
nodes.norm_label: phase 3b: rewrite a deleted-remote conflict to the delete-vs-changed shape

nodes.label: Phase 3c: on ETag mismatch refresh and re-decide instead of throwing
nodes.rationale: The guard is right to exist; its failure mode was wrong. Re-probe, re-download the snapshot, compare with what the user was shown: identical bytes proceed, different content re-presents the dialog. Retry bounded to 2 attempts so a pathologically hot file surfaces rather than spinning.
nodes.norm_label: phase 3c: on etag mismatch refresh and re-decide instead of throwing

nodes.label: Phase 3d: the dialog preselects nothing where a default could destroy the newer side
nodes.rationale: Observed on daily/2026-08-21.typ: unconditional keep-local would have silently deleted an appended line; only reading byte counts caught it. A default that can destroy the strictly-newer side is the wrong default on a data-safety screen. Label options by relationship ('adds 1 line'), not raw byte counts.
nodes.norm_label: phase 3d: the dialog preselects nothing where a default could destroy the newer side

nodes.label: Phase 4: never fail invisibly; resolve in bulk
nodes.rationale: Ships with Phase 3 rather than after, because the invisible-failure half is a data-safety concern, not polish.
nodes.norm_label: phase 4: never fail invisibly; resolve in bulk

nodes.label: syncError banner losing its slot to the 'Syncing…' card
nodes.rationale: An error caught into a slot occupied by another card is an error nobody ever sees.
nodes.norm_label: syncerror banner losing its slot to the 'syncing...' card

nodes.label: Unkeyed positional conflict rows
nodes.rationale: A reload between frames moved a different record under the finger — one of the two real mechanisms behind 'resolving does nothing'.

nodes.label: Correction: the swallowed-tap theory was wrong
nodes.rationale: The dashboard does not listen to syncProgressTick; it repaints from its own 500 ms timer and a test already proved a tap lands during a sync. The real causes were the invisible error and unkeyed rows.
nodes.norm_label: correction: the swallowed-tap theory was wrong

nodes.label: Correction: the claimed sync_conflicts fixtures never existed
nodes.rationale: Coverage is behavioural instead, each test written to fail on the code it replaced.
nodes.norm_label: correction: the claimed sync_conflicts fixtures never existed

nodes.label: article-pipeline drain (rewrites articles/*.typ continuously)
nodes.rationale: A device holding an older copy of a file the drain has since rewritten gets a first-sync-different conflict even though nobody edited anything on the device.

nodes.label: Findings from the 0.3.0+93 device rollout — scope of work
nodes.norm_label: findings from the 0.3.0+93 device rollout — scope of work

nodes.label: Shared index / 'hard computing on the laptop'
nodes.rationale: One machine does the expensive Typst inspection; every other device reuses it via a donor index in _system/index/<deviceId>.json, matched by content hash, so phones never recompile what the laptop already compiled. In reality the strongest CPU in the fleet did none of the work and the weakest ones did all of it.
nodes.norm_label: shared index / 'hard computing on the laptop'

nodes.label: 1a: the laptop produces no index at all
nodes.rationale: Indexing lives in the app, but the machine doing the writing is the Python drain, which never indexes. Fix: move donor publication into tylog_core so the CLI emits one under a stable per-machine deviceId, run as the drain's post-step.
nodes.norm_label: 1a: the laptop produces no index at all

nodes.label: 1b: a schema bump invalidates every donor at once
nodes.rationale: The v8→v9 bump was a derivation change (kind aliased into tags) and the Typst query output was byte-identical, yet every donor died — precisely when reuse matters most it is guaranteed to fail. Donor grows roughly 2× when storing raw records; measure before committing.
nodes.norm_label: 1b: a schema bump invalidates every donor at once

nodes.label: 1c: stale donors are never collected
nodes.rationale: Four dead v8/schema-1 donors (5.7 MB) plus two live v9 ones (13 MB) sit in _system/, which is inside the sync allowlist, so every device downloads every donor forever, most permanently unusable.

nodes.label: 1d: donor reuse fails silently
nodes.rationale: Nothing reported whether reuse happened; it had been dead for at least two days and would have stayed dead indefinitely — it only surfaced because it was asked about directly.

nodes.label: 2: notes referencing not-yet-synced assets fall back unnecessarily
nodes.rationale: The placeholder work substituted only for assets that exist in the vault listing; the case that matters on a syncing device is a referenced-but-missing path. Supply the placeholder for the reference, not for the file — but a genuinely broken note must still be reported, not silently fixed.
nodes.norm_label: 2: notes referencing not-yet-synced assets fall back unnecessarily

nodes.label: 3: orphan temp files left by the atomic-write path
nodes.rationale: .index.json.tylog-*.tmp and .sync_state.json.tylog-*.backup survive interrupted writes; swept at vault open after an hour untouched.
nodes.norm_label: 3: orphan temp files left by the atomic-write path

nodes.label: 3: drain junk gate misses redirect/404 pages
nodes.rationale: Scraper artefacts that should never have become articles; belongs to the article-pipeline repo (junk_reason + length floor) but is the source of the conflict churn.
nodes.norm_label: 3: drain junk gate misses redirect/404 pages

nodes.label: 3: a stray keystroke materialises a daily note
nodes.rationale: The old behaviour also left the editor permanently dirty, which disabled idle maintenance and midnight rollover. Emptying a file that was never a structured note now deletes it; a real note still refuses.
nodes.norm_label: 3: a stray keystroke materialises a daily note

nodes.label: Donor version gate: indexVersion != kVaultIndexVersion → skip
nodes.norm_label: donor version gate: indexversion != kvaultindexversion → skip

nodes.label: Image placeholder pre-seeded into the VFS
nodes.norm_label: image placeholder pre-seeded into the vfs

nodes.label: Sync stage timings measured on the P30 (18.1 s no-transfer pass)
nodes.rationale: scan-local 9348 ms, list-remote 5590, prepare-remote-folder 1180, probe-root 778, sync-file for all 11,610 files just 96 ms.
nodes.norm_label: sync stage timings measured on the p30 (18.1 s no-transfer pass)

nodes.label: Two planned optimisations retired by measurement
nodes.rationale: Partitioning unchanged paths out of the per-file loop and making the 5 s checkpoint O(changed) both targeted 96 ms of 18,100; the checkpoint never fires in a no-change pass. The '~1,440 checkpoint writes per pass' figure came from reasoning about a 2-hour transferring pass and does not describe the common case.
nodes.norm_label: two planned optimisations retired by measurement

nodes.label: The local tree was walked twice per pass
nodes.rationale: The no-change shortcut takes a full recursive listing, discards it on any mismatch, and scan-local immediately re-walks the identical tree; only a network PROPFIND separates them, so the snapshot is the same either way.
nodes.norm_label: the local tree was walked twice per pass

nodes.label: A guaranteed-405 MKCOL per run
nodes.rationale: prepare-remote-folder ran above the shortcut; moved below it but still above list-remote so a folder that really vanished is recreated on the full path.

nodes.label: SafBridge recursive listing (one ContentResolver.query per directory)
nodes.rationale: Nothing caches it across calls — the indexer (scanner.dart:417), the validator (validation.dart:61) and the backup sweep each re-walk the same tree afterwards.
nodes.norm_label: safbridge recursive listing (one contentresolver.query per directory)

nodes.label: Proposed: share one directory listing between sync and the scan that follows
nodes.rationale: Cheapest option, invalidated on any local write; bounded risk is that a stale listing must never hide a file. The ContentObserver alternative is a bigger native change and SAF change notifications are not guaranteed granular, so it needs a fallback walk on a timer.
nodes.norm_label: proposed: share one directory listing between sync and the scan that follows
